canonical_statement: For p > 0, a complex-valued almost-everywhere convergent sequence on an arbitrary measure space whose p-power densities are integrable with uniformly bounded integrals satisfies the Brezis-Lieb integral splitting limit.
domain_and_universes: universe u; alpha : Type u; MeasurableSpace alpha; mu : Measure alpha; p : Real; f : alpha -> Complex; fseq : Nat -> alpha -> Complex; Prop in universe 0
hypotheses: for every n, fseq n is AEStronglyMeasurable with respect to mu
fseq n tends to f pointwise mu-almost everywhere
there is one real C bounding the integrals of all p-power densities, each of which is Integrable
conclusion: Tendsto (integral |fseq n|^p - integral |fseq n - f|^p) atTop (nhds (integral |f|^p)), with powers encoded by Real.rpow of the complex norm.

encoding_decisions.scalar: Complex; the real-valued form follows by a later checked scalar transport and is not substituted here
encoding_decisions.power: Real.rpow (norm z) p, retaining the source range p > 0 rather than restricting to norm exponents p >= 1
encoding_decisions.integral: Bochner integral of a nonnegative real density
encoding_decisions.finite_mass: Each density is explicitly Integrable, avoiding Lean's zero value for the integral of a nonintegrable function
encoding_decisions.uniform_bound: One C is existentially quantified before all sequence indices
encoding_decisions.measure_space: Arbitrary Measure alpha; no finite or sigma-finite strengthening

killed: strengthened almost-everywhere convergence to everywhere convergence
changed the complex scalar domain to real
moved the integral bound after the sequence index

boundary_and_exclusions: p = 0 and p < 0 are excluded; 0 < p < 1 remains included
Null sets are respected through almost-everywhere convergence
No finite-measure or sigma-finite hypothesis is introduced
No Lp-space or p >= 1 restricted corollary is credited as the canonical theorem
status_boundary: This freezes and kernel-elaborates the exact selected Brezis-Lieb target with a definitional expansion and four structural mutations. It supplies no proof, anchor acceptance, source-fidelity acceptance, or theorem-completion evidence.
